  "title": "Temporary Partners",
  "description": "Expanded Series Bible III #3 Temporary Partners reusable adult idea source: pairs two adults for one finite assigned task such as a project, work contract, competition, investigation, booth, trip or event duty. The engine generates who assigned the pair, prior history, working friction, stakes and open endings without matchmaking assumptions.",
  "source_version": "1.0",
  "bible": {
    "document": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible III",
    "version": "0.4",
    "entry": "3",
    "kind": "series"
  },
  "summary": "Adult {{char}} and {{user}} are assigned to complete one finite task together — a university project, work assignment, competition, investigation, training exercise, convention booth, tournament, research trip, event duty or similar job — by somebody or something other than romantic matchmaking. The engine is the bounded collaboration itself: real work with a real deadline, two adults who may be strangers, rivals, acquaintances or ex-partners, complementary or conflicting skills, and a partnership with a defined end date. Being assigned together establishes neither attraction nor compatibility, and the task must remain meaningful rather than an excuse to put two people in a room. The story may end cleanly, in friendship, in rivalry, in a practical reason to stay in contact, or in something the characters themselves have not yet decided; {{user}}'s reactions and every outcome remain open.",
  "core_premise": "Two adults are paired for a finite task without romantic matchmaking being the reason: a university project, work assignment, competition, investigation, training exercise, convention booth, tournament, research trip, event duty, or similar job. Somebody or something assigns the pairing — lecturer, manager, organiser, draw, client, roster or circumstance — and the task carries real stakes and a real end point. The collaboration does not predetermine attraction, friendship or any other relationship change; the two adults may end the task as polite strangers, rivals, friends, partners who stay in contact, or anything the roleplay supports. The task must remain meaningful, and whether the partnership ends cleanly or creates a reason to stay in contact is open.",
  "setup": "Establish the finite task concretely: what the job is, who assigned the pair and why, how long it lasts, what the external deadline and stakes are, and how well the two adults knew each other beforehand. Give {{char}} her own competence, working style, outside life and attitude toward the assignment, and give {{user}} a clear role in the task without scripting his feelings, reactions or decisions. Open the roleplay at or near the point where the pairing becomes active — the first planning meeting, the assignment announcement, the first shared shift or the first day of travel — with the outcome of the task and of the relationship completely unwritten.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Who paired them: lecturer, manager, coach, organiser, random draw, client request, roster, bureaucratic error or circumstance.",
    "What the finite task is: university project, work assignment, competition entry, investigation, training exercise, convention booth, tournament, research trip, event duty or another bounded job.",
    "Length of the task: one afternoon, one weekend, one shift, one season, one semester or one contract.",
    "Whether {{char}} and {{user}} knew one another beforehand, and whether that history is friendly, hostile, romantic or second-hand.",
    "Complementary versus conflicting skills and working styles, including who actually leads.",
    "External deadline and how hard it is: exam board, client, match day, weather window or only their own standards.",
    "Stakes for success: shared marks, employment, prize money, reputation, safety, somebody else's budget or a personal dream.",
    "Whether either adult resents the pairing, and whether they say so openly or keep it private.",
    "Attitudes on day one: enthusiasm, indifference, scepticism, professional courtesy, or open resentment from one or both sides.",
    "What complications intrude: rival pairs, meddling assigners, outside offers, resource shortages, rule changes, third parties or existing partners.",
    "What the working dynamic actually becomes under pressure, separate from either adult's intentions.",
    "Whether each adult's private life leaks into the task, and how the other responds.",
    "How the task ends: success, partial result or shared failure, and how much of that is decided before the final day.",
    "Whether the partnership ends cleanly or creates a practical reason to stay in contact.",
    "What, if anything, either adult wants from the other beyond the task, and whether they ever say so.",
    "Whether any relationship change — friendship, rivalry, tension, romance or nothing at all — develops, which remains open."
  ],
  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions, future behaviour, competence or reactions unless the selected concept explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep assumptions, reputations, rumours and objective ground truth distinct where relevant.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave cooperation, refusal, conflict, friendship, romance, exposure, quitting and other player choices open.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Being assigned together does not establish attraction, compatibility or friendship. The pairing is a work arrangement, not a matchmaking device.",
    "The task must remain meaningful rather than serving only as an excuse to put two people in a room. Give the job real stakes, real methods and real obstacles.",
    "Do not force romance into this series. Practical partnership, friendship, rivalry, unresolved tension, casual sex between consenting adults or no relationship change at all are all valid outcomes.",
    "Assignment, cohabitation during a task, shared travel, late nights or one bed created by logistics do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy, if it ever occurs, must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement or boundaries.",
    "Deadlines create urgency, not a mandated confession, breakdown, romance or sex scene. Working through the night can simply be work.",
    "Roles do not remove autonomy: the assigned lead, assistant, expert or novice can negotiate, disagree, refuse or quit like any adult.",
    "Whether the pair works well or badly together should vary independently of whether they like each other.",
    "Let both adults be competent or flawed in mixed, believable ways; do not make one the saviour and the other the burden by default.",
    "{{user}}'s working ability, motives and future are not predetermined; a partner's low or high opinion of him is her belief, not canon.",
    "Keep ground truth separate from character rationalisation. A partner who takes credit, hides a mistake or resents the assignment may justify it; the narration does not endorse the justification.",
    "Characters should remain people outside their hook. The task is important to them without being the only thing they talk about.",
    "Prior history, if any, should complicate the working relationship rather than guaranteeing its direction.",
    "Vary who requested whom, who resents whom and who works harder; none of these proves anything about feelings.",
    "Third parties — assigners, rivals, inspectors, existing partners — may interfere, but their interference does not decide the outcome.",
    "The finite task should have a defined shape: a start, a middle of real work, and an end point the story can actually reach.",
    "Do not manufacture a dramatic hidden reason for every ordinary pairing; bureaucratic randomness is a valid origin.",
    "Keep any intimate content non-graphic and open at a playable moment in the working relationship."
  ],
  "guardrails": [
    "All participants in any romantic or sexual content are adults.",
    "The pairing exists for the task, and the task must remain real work with real stakes.",
    "No predetermination of {{user}}'s speech, feelings, competence, consent, decisions or future.",
    "Assigned partnership, shared shifts, travel, accommodation or late nights do not create blanket consent for anything.",
    "Consent is activity-specific and can be withdrawn; a working relationship grants no access to anyone's body or private life.",
    "Do not force romance, friendship or rivalry where the generated concept does not support it; no relationship change is a valid outcome.",
    "Beliefs about {{user}}'s ability, motives or prospects are {{char}}'s assessments, not objective canon.",
    "Both adults retain full autonomy: either can renegotiate, complain, refuse tasks, report problems or quit the partnership.",
    "Third-party interference, sabotage or pressure does not excuse characters from their own choices.",
    "Existing partners, managers or institutions do not own either adult's private life or decisions.",
    "Keep intimate elements non-graphic, foreground the practical work and interpersonal meaning.",
    "{{char}} keeps her own career, skills, hobbies, family, friends, values and boundaries beyond the task."

  "diversity_axes": [
    "Who paired them: lecturer, manager, coach, organiser, random draw, client, agency, roster, error or circumstance.",
    "The task itself: project, work contract, competition, investigation, booth, tournament, research trip, event duty, training, production or delivery.",
    "Duration: one afternoon, one shift, one weekend, one month, one season, one semester or one contract.",
    "Prior history: strangers, name-recognition, old classmates, rivals, ex-partners, ex-coworkers, online acquaintances, mentor and student or childhood friends.",
    "Skills: complementary specialists, identical skills, expert and novice, or mismatched methods that somehow work.",
    "Deadline hardness: external and immovable, internal and soft, or moved mid-task.",
    "Stakes: shared marks, employment, prize, reputation, safety, someone else's money or a personal dream.",
    "Attitudes on assignment: mutual resentment, one-sided reluctance, professional courtesy, enthusiasm or indifference.",
    "Whether either adult requested the pairing, and whether the other knows.",
    "Complications: rival pairs, meddling assigners, outside offers, rule changes, resource shortages or existing partners.",
    "Setting: campus, small office, trades, field station, convention, sports club, kitchen, rural town, remote online, historical period, vessel or expedition.",
    "Working dynamic under pressure: friction that resolves, friction that never resolves, or unexpectedly smooth collaboration.",
    "How the task ends: success, partial result, failure or early termination.",
    "Whether the partnership ends cleanly, stays a friendship, becomes a recurring arrangement or creates a reason to keep in contact.",
    "Whether any romance or tension ever develops, which is never mandatory and always requires mutual choice."

    {
      "id": "trigger",
      "content": "Decide who paired them and why: lecturer, manager, coach, draw, client, roster, error or circumstance. The origin shapes expectations and resentments but never the outcome."
    },
    {
      "id": "task",
      "content": "Make the task concrete and bounded: deliverable, method, resources and end date. It must be meaningful on its own terms rather than an excuse for proximity."
    },
    {
      "id": "history",
      "content": "Vary what the pair knew of each other beforehand, from total strangers to ex-partners. Prior history should complicate the collaboration without dictating its direction."
    },
    {
      "id": "skills",
      "content": "Give the two adults separate competences and working styles — complementary, identical, mismatched or in conflict. Let the work reveal character rather than announce compatibility."
    },
    {
      "id": "pressure",
      "content": "Choose a deadline and stakes proportionate to the concept: shared marks, employment, safety, reputation or a dream. Pressure creates urgency, not mandated drama."
    },
    {
      "id": "attitudes",
      "content": "Let each adult hold a specific attitude toward the pairing — enthusiasm, resentment, courtesy, scepticism — and let those attitudes change or hold as the evidence of actual work arrives."
    },
    {
      "id": "third",
      "content": "Outside parties — assigners, rivals, inspectors, helpers with agendas, existing partners — may intrude on the pairing. Interference creates material; it does not decide the ending."

    {
      "id": "character",
      "content": "{{char}} keeps her own skills, goals, hobbies, obligations and boundaries beyond the task. The job matters to her without being the only thing she is."

      "id": "user",
      "content": "Give {{user}} a clear role in the task and working competence appropriate to the concept, but never script his feelings, effort, reactions or decisions. Others' opinions of him are beliefs, not canon."

      "id": "ending",
      "content": "The task has a defined end. Whether the pair parts cleanly, fails together, keeps a practical reason to stay in contact or transforms into something else is open roleplay space."

    {
      "id": "opening",

    {
      "id": "boundary",
      "content": "Distinct from Set Up Together, whose pairings are engineered by friends for social ends; the assignment here exists for the task. Natural crossovers include I Need an Expert, Before We Go Home, Study Together, Train With Me, Workplace Stories and We Used to Know Each Other."

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for Temporary Partners. Adult {{char}} and {{user}} are assigned to one finite task — university project, work contract, competition, investigation, training exercise, convention booth, tournament, research trip or event duty — by a lecturer, manager, draw, client or circumstance rather than matchmaking. Vary the task and its length, who assigned the pair, prior history from strangers to exes, complementary or conflicting skills, deadlines and real stakes, each adult's attitude toward the assignment, and any third-party complications. Being paired establishes neither attraction nor compatibility; the task must stay meaningful work, and friendship, rivalry, practical partnership, tension or no change are all valid endings. Never script {{user}}'s feelings, effort or decisions; keep consent, boundaries and every outcome open, including whether the partnership ends cleanly or creates a reason to stay in contact."
